posts.cooked: I'd buy a solo version of EVE for €100... I swear!!!
play eve online for a few then gives the itch for Imperium....

You won't be able to run a solo version of EVE.

EVE requires a server cluster to run. It's not just a single executable that you launch. It's many individual instances and control nodes being run on separate hardware (or virtual machines). It would require a fundamental restructuring of the software that would cost millions of dollars to accomplish, which would be the same as throwing the money into a pit, as the handful of people interested in something like this wouldn't offset the development cost with their hundred-Euro pittances.

I'd pay $50 per month, or even more for a good MMO, if everyone was paying the same and on equal grounds.

Even $100 per month is only a bit more than $25 per week. If that's what it takes to escape this ♥♥♥♥, I'd be happy to, and I doubt I'm alone.

you'll never be on the same equal grounds though, either people will have started before you, or they simply play more than you.

what you'd be looking for is a game that not only has a fixed amount of money you can put into it, but also a fixed amount of time per day. THEN it would be 'Equal Grounds'. (but you'd still ofc have those who can play for the full amount of time and those who can only play for half of that time, even within those barriers there would be a disparity)

because in a game where what you do and how much time you spend doing it directly impacts the outcome it stands to reason then that those who spend the most time doing it will have the most advantage or get the most out of it.

if I can play the game all day every day, but you can only play the game for 2-4 hours each day after work, is it an 'equal grounds' situation. most people can't just pull out more time in the same way they can't just pull out more money. the whole concept of an equal playing field doesn't really exist. in this hypothetical $100 a month MMO would still have rampant RMT. (if people are willing to spend $100 a month on a sub then the sky is the limit on the level of RMT that group of people would be open to, you'd be playing an mmo with the whaleyst whales)

but its the same problem though right, if its not one thing its another, this idea of a perfectly balanced playing field where I'm progressing in the game at the same rate as you at all times is a pipe dream, no matter the game, how about you piss off to this imaginary game that doesn't exist?

one of the first games I played online was diablo 2, from maybe 2002 to 2005, this game wasn't competitive, it had its ladders but its not a pvp focused game. still had rampant RMT. those who Want to pay to get ahead, don't care if the rules say its OK or not. that is the problem. just having an mmo with an obnoxiously high subscription price isn't some sort of silver bullet cure all to balanced game play.

but it is though, the idea is that Eve's monetisation, and plex to isk is imbalanced, people can dump 1000s of dollar on plex and have more 'stuff' to lose than someone who didn't do that.

this person also needs to sink the time into the game to actually make use of that plex to isk conversion. will they come out on top, its largely dependant on them.

but that is the balance point for Eve, you either have time or money, its pretty rare that people have both of those things, like retired people with huge pensions maybe, most people either have a lot of free time (limited disposable income), because they are unemployed or work part time, are simply disabled and can't work so have a lot of free time. however most people of working age have a full time job, so if you're lucky and also don't have children you maybe get 4-5 hours per day to play the game. you could spend that grinding ISK but maybe you'd rather not do that.

ultimately that is the battle and the balance struggle its the no lifers vs the people with lives. you're either sitting there all day grinding ISK because you have the free time to do that. or you're not able to do that. because you don't have the time. the only way then to make up that disparity would be to sell plex so that you don't have to grind or waste the few precious hours you have to play that day, grinding.

its really not that difficult to understand.

there will always be many people playing the game constantly all day, every day, 12hrs +, they'll wake up, login and play all day until they fall asleep. and do that the next day and the next day. there is no way to make up for this level of dedication. if you too also can't sink that same amount of time into the game (again, no matter the game, its not exclusive to Eve)

the plex system is currently also ofc, maintaining its F2P ability. the people you're selling plex to are the no lifers who can't afford to buy omega (or just don't want to spend their own money on it) the people getting the ISK are the ones who don't have time to grind. its a circle. the no lifers sell ISK to the people with lives, the people with lives sell plex to the no lifers so they can be omega. its self sustaining in this way. because there will always be people with tonnes of free time, and there will also be people with a bunch of disposable income and not as much free time.

as far as i'm concerned if someone wants to sell plex and buy ships, I just see that as content being created, which is what it boils down to. people selling plex stirs the market, you're often selling plex to get isk to buy something like a ship, so several things are happening there, 1) a new ship is now in space that wasn't there before 2) the people who mined the minerals and build the ship and then sold it, got paid 3) modules were sold to fit to that ship which also probably touches several indy chains 4) pvpers are happy because there is another ship flying around.

in terms of the impact on the game, selling plex just stimulates the market, and almost always leads to content being created in some form. even if that is just another ship flying around that wasn't there before.

you have to keep in mind that billions of ISK sitting in wallets and 100s of ships sitting in stations are largely impacting nothing if its not on the field shooting at your enemies. in other words it doesn't really matter how wealthy you are when you can only realistically field so much of your wealth at any given time. if you're fielding 10s of billions of isk you're probably in a capital fight with other people also fielding 10s of billions of isk. if you're fielding sub 1b isk, you're probably fighting people also risking sub 1b isk. I have close to maybe 50b isk worth of ships in total but I can't field 50b isk worth of ships at the same time. how much you have doesn't automatically translate into a tangible advantage if you can't effectively make use of it. when you undock a ship in Eve, that is what you're working with, in most cases you won't be able to reship and make it back to a fight that you're still winning. so what you bring is what you have and any other ships or isk are largely irrelevant and can't help you change the outcome.

X3's background simulation was pretty interesting for the time, and you can build stations and have npcs come a long and buy things then sell them else where. the OoS (out of sector) simulation was pretty basic though. I don't think astrox does this anymore either I think it used to simulate systems that you weren't in, or had stations in. but most of them aren't progressing if you aren't there (well the dude working on astrox has sort of stopped working on it afaik), like avorion, that had simulated sectors like X3 but I think they scaled it back because it was too buggy and taxing. now you just send your AI ships off on missions that happen in the background, rather than the game simulating whole sectors.

I remember large capital ship battles in X3 often working out better in your favour if you weren't in system and the out comes of battles could vary wildly depending on if you let it simulate it or you sat there and watched it play out.
